first.rationale: Verify the onboarding result because it directly addresses both current declines and could improve sustainable qualified revenue without immediately sacrificing price realization. Verify promotional pricing because the competitor threat makes it consequential, but its long-term revenue and customer-quality effects are less certain. Run a standard, tightly measured onboarding simplification experiment while monitoring activation, qualified conversion, retention proxies, and revenue per account; avoid assuming pricing is the best response until verified.

mid.rationale: Run a standard, tightly measured onboarding simplification experiment. The verified record shows completion improved 13%, time-to-value fell 2.1 days, and 30-day retention rose 3%, directly addressing the current onboarding and activation declines while supporting sustainable qualified revenue. Do not use broad discounting as the primary response: although it lifted qualified revenue 18% initially, retention fell 12% and the cohort failed to survive the first renewal cycle. Measure completion, activation, time-to-value, qualified revenue, and retention before scaling.

final2.rationale: Keep the onboarding simplification decision rather than pivoting to an unverified price cut under competitive pressure. The verified onboarding result improves completion, time-to-value, and 30-day retention, directly addressing current funnel deterioration and supporting sustainable qualified revenue. Do not deploy broad promotional pricing: the verified discount increased near-term qualified revenue but reduced 30-day retention 12% and failed at first renewal. Treat the deeper competitor cut as a reason to monitor price-sensitive churn and segment economics urgently, not as sufficient evidence to choose an action that risks downstream value.
